images.alt: A Macintosh Quadra 800 desktop computer case, a beige tower-style Macintosh from 1993
images.caption: A Macintosh Quadra 800 — the 1993 machine this exhibit's Mac OS 7.5.3 boots from, built around Motorola's 68040.

images.alt: An Apple Macintosh Quadra 800 computer, beige case, photographed for a computer museum collection
images.caption: The Quadra 800 was the last and fastest of the 68000-family Macintoshes, the line every Mac had used since 1984.

images.alt: A Macintosh Quadra 700 on display at the Apple Museum in Prague
images.caption: A sibling model, the Quadra 700 of 1991, from the same 68040-based generation of Macintosh workstations.

images.alt: A Macintosh Quadra 610 desktop computer, a compact beige case Macintosh from the early 1990s
images.caption: The Quadra 610's compact case shows how far the same 68040-based family stretched, from tower to pizza-box.

images.alt: The interior of a Macintosh Quadra 605, showing its logic board and 68040-family components
images.caption: Inside the case: the Motorola 68040 logic board that ran System 7.5.3, the last processor family classic Mac OS ever used.
